boundary_test.prompt: Changed boundary: 8m-by-15m rectangle, but direct interior shortcut is CLOSED; only two adjacent edges may be used. With a 20m cap, is any allowed route possible? Decide independently.
boundary_test.answer: No. Straight diagonal17m would pass20m but is forbidden; permitted boundary walk8+15=23m exceeds cap, so neither eligible.
boundary_test.confirms: A valid geometric distance still fails if its route is forbidden, so check access as well as length.

questions.stem: A rectangle has perpendicular sides 9m and12m. To get from one corner to the opposite one you may cross the straight diagonal or walk along TWO adjacent edges. Travel allowance is AT MOST18m. Retrieve the right-triangle distance relation and calculate BOTH routes. Which route(s) satisfy the allowance, and how many metres does the shorter route save? Explain why d² is not itself a measured length.
conditions: Endpoints are opposite corners; direct diagonal OR two adjacent edges are potential routes.
Wholly original authored TEST, no source admission.
questions.failure_signal: Confuses d²=225 with225m, uses full perimeter42m, or skips allowance.

answer.summary: Diagonal15m, boundary21m, direct only within18m, saving6m.
reasoning: Use Pythagoras d²=9²+12²=225, hence diagonal d=15m.
The two-edge route is9+12=21m, not full perimeter.
The shortcut saves21−15=6m; d² has squared-length units.

questions.stem: Reverse case: the DIRECT diagonal of a rectangle is13m and one perpendicular side5m; other side unknown. Reach opposite corners either straight across or along TWO adjacent sides. Travel limit15m. Retrieve the right-triangle relation IN REVERSE to find the missing side, calculate both paths, decide which passes limit and saving. Why would adding 13²+5² be incorrect?
conditions: Diagonal13m known, one perpendicular side5m known, other side unknown.
Straight direct route or exactly two adjacent sides.

hints.text: Which given segment is hypotenuse and which is a leg? Recall that the hypotenuse has the largest square; decide what to subtract.

questions.failure_signal: Wrongly add13²+5² as if both were legs, or omit cap.

answer.summary: Missing side12m; direct13m, boundary17m; only direct within15m, saves4m.
reasoning: The hypotenuse13m is known: 13²=5²+b²; b²=169−25=144, b=12m.
13≤15<17: only direct route qualifies and saves4m.
Adding13² and5² would wrongly treat known hypotenuse as a leg.
